notes: How this part was researched: the session's shared web-search allowance ran out after six searches (the six county candidates at the top of the list). Everything else was read by opening pages directly with the kit's honest User-Agent (states/net.py), each host's robots.txt read first and obeyed, or with the page-reading tool where a campaign site answered the script with 429. No search engine was read in place of the search tool.

Campaign websites for House Democrats were learned from the Iowa House Democrats' own candidate pages (https://iowahouse.org/candidates-page-1 and -page-2), which give each candidate's district, town, committee and site; each site was then opened and kept only where its own pages name the candidate and the office. That caucus list is not recorded as an endorsement: it is a list of the party's candidates, not a published endorsement.

Mike Naig's endorsed_by entry is the Republican Party of Iowa's own '2026 Candidates' page, which lists him for Secretary of Agriculture. It is a list of the party's nominees and does not use the word 'endorse'. Left for the second reader to judge; delete it if a nominee list is not to count.

Bill Dotzler: the Iowa Legislature's page is for Senator William A. Dotzler Jr., Democrat, District 31. No page that this script may read says in so many words that he is this year's Black Hawk County supervisor candidate: KWWL and KCRG reported it, but both sites' robots.txt ask Claude's readers to stay out, so nothing is cited from them. The tie is the name, the state and the party. Left for the second reader to judge.

Luana Stoltenberg: Wikipedia's article is for the Republican who represented Iowa House District 81 from 2023 to 2025 and lives in Davenport (Scott County). No page read says in so many words that she is this year's Scott County supervisor candidate; the tie is the name, the state, the party and the place. Left for the second reader to judge.
sokoforiowa.com (the address the Iowa House Democrats give for Keith Soko, House District 93) answered with a CAPTCHA page; it was left alone and no website is recorded for him.

Robots: thegazette.com, kwwl.com, kcrg.com and iowacapitaldispatch.com ask Claude's readers to stay out, so nothing is cited from them (this includes The Gazette's candidate page for Sue Dvorsky and the Capital Dispatch story on Kimberly Graham's 2021 announcement). A KWWL page was opened once through a shared helper script before its robots.txt had been checked; nothing from it is recorded.

robertgreenway.com resolves but answered the script with 429 and the page-reading tool could not reach it, so it was not seen and nothing is recorded for Robert Greenway. williamsforiowa.com answered with a self-signed certificate and was not read.

Heather Sievers's home page is titled 'Home | Sievers 2026' and does not name the office; her About page speaks of 'her first run for Iowa House of Representatives' although Wikipedia's 2024 table shows a Heather Sievers as the Democratic candidate in the same district (House District 40) in 2024. Both are recorded; the second reader may wish to look at that wording.

Jennifer Kirkman's site says she has volunteered with the Burlington Library Board among other organizations, without a post or years; no office is recorded from it. Thomas O'Donnell's site names no public office. Sue Dvorsky's past chairmanship of the Iowa Democratic Party is a party post, not a public office, and is not recorded.

Sitting legislators (Craig Williams, Devon Wood, David Young, Sean Bagniewski, David Blom, Eric Gjerde, Daniel Gosa): no campaign website of their own and no party endorsement page was found. The Iowa House Democrats' pages link only to the caucus's own spotlight pages for Bagniewski, Gjerde and Gosa; the Iowa House Republicans' and Senate Republicans' sites carry no candidate list.

Nothing citable was found for: Robert Greenway, Travis A Inghram (Des Moines County's attorney page does not name him), Sue Dvorsky (Johnson County's supervisor districts page lists her as a District 3 candidate, which our record already shows), Martin Chitty, Mandy Newton Rosenow (the caucus page gives no site), Keith Soko, Ronald Langston, Jim Vowels, Rachel Gravert, and the seven sitting legislators.
No full birth date is recorded: both dates seen (Dotzler, Naig) are from Wikipedia, so only the year is kept.

Second reader, 2026-10-02: every address was opened again (the kit's honest fetch; the page-reading tool for the two sites that answer scripts with 429; Linn County's PDF read as text). Kept: 32 findings. Removed: all five of Bill Dotzler's (no readable page ties the senator to the supervisor race) and Mike Naig's party listing (a candidate list, not an endorsement). Luana Stoltenberg's are kept on the state, the party and Davenport in Scott County, all in the one article. One wording corrected (Jeff Thurlow's website note).
